itemdesc-wire-*: A coil of drawn wire. Needed for dynamos, motors and power lines.
blockdesc-wiredrawing-*: A bench for drawing metal rods into wire.
itemdesc-drawdie-*: A plate with a sized hole that wire is pulled through. Part of the wire-drawing bench.
itemdesc-gearrack-*: A toothed bar that the carriage pinion rolls along. Part of the wire-drawing bench.
itemdesc-pinion-*: A gear on the crank axle: it rolls along the gear rack and pulls the carriage. Part of the wire-drawing bench.
blockdesc-rollingmill-*: A hand-cranked mill with two steel rolls. The smooth part of the rolls flattens an ingot into a sheet, the grooves turn it into rods.
machine-drive-hand: Driven by crank, axle connects from the {0}
itemdesc-rolledsheet-*: A thin sheet rolled from an ingot on a rolling mill. Flatter and thinner than a forged plate.
itemdesc-millroll-*: A hardened steel cylinder with a gear on its axle. Part of the rolling mill, you need two.
itemdesc-screwdown-*: A bridge with screws and bronze gears that sets the gap between the rolls. Part of the rolling mill.
handbook-wiredrawing-text:
Wire-drawing bench
A machine that pulls a metal rod through a sized hole (a draw die) to make wire.

Building it
1. Craft a wire-drawing bench frame on a workbench: three planks on top and two sticks on each side. Place it: the bench takes two blocks in length.
2. Finish it with right clicks while holding the part, one stage at a time:
• 4 iron rods: the frame rails;
• a gear rack;
• a draw die;
• 2 iron plates: the carriage body;
• a wire-drawing pinion: the crank with its gear.
Look at the bench to see what the next stage needs.
3. The gear rack, draw die and pinion are forged on an anvil from an iron ingot.
Breaking the bench returns the frame and some of the parts.

Using it
Right click the bench to open its window. Put a rod into the input slot, close the window, look at the crank and hold right click: the carriage moves along the rack and pulls the rod through the die. Let go and the work pauses, then continues from the same point. Wire appears in the output slot. You can only take items out of the output slot.

What it draws
Copper rod → copper wire, 5 seconds.

Rods are cheaper to make on a rolling mill: it turns one ingot into two.
handbook-rollingmill-text:
Rolling mill
A hand-cranked mill with two steel rolls. The smooth part of the rolls flattens an ingot into a thin sheet, the grooves turn it into rods.

Building it
1. Craft a rolling mill stand on a workbench, a wooden table: three planks on top; a stick, iron nails and strips and a stick below. Place it.
2. Finish it with right clicks while holding the part:
• 2 iron plates: the mill housing;
• 2 mill rolls;
• a screwdown: the bridge with screws and gears;
• an iron rod: the crank.
3. Mill rolls are forged on an anvil from a steel ingot, the screwdown from tin bronze.
Breaking the mill returns the stand and some of the parts.

Using it
Right click the mill to open its window. Use the buttons at the bottom to pick "Sheet" or "Rods". Put an ingot into the input slot, close the window, look at the crank on the side and hold right click: the rolls start turning. Switching the mode in the middle of rolling starts it over.

Axle power
You can connect a mechanical power axle, for example from a windmill, to the crank side. The crank then comes off, a coupling takes its place, and the mill rolls on its own while the axle turns. The faster the axle, the faster the rolling. Remove the axle and the crank comes back.

What it rolls
Sheet mode: ingot → 1 sheet, 6 seconds.
Rods mode: ingot → 2 rods, 4 seconds.
Metals: copper, tin bronze, iron, steel.

A rolled sheet is flatter and thinner than a forged plate. Rods go to the wire-drawing bench.
wiredrawing-handbook-build-text:
Place the frame and finish it with right clicks while holding the part, in this order:
1. 4 iron rods
2. A gear rack
3. A draw die
4. 2 iron plates
5. A wire-drawing pinion
The gear rack, draw die and pinion are forged on an anvil from an iron ingot.
wiredrawing-handbook-use-text:
Right click the bench to open its window. Put a rod into the input slot, look at the crank and hold right click.
Instead of the crank you can bring a mechanical power axle to the end of the bench with the drawing die: the crank comes off and a lead screw pulls the carriage on its own while the axle turns.
More: the Wire-drawing bench guide.
rollingmill-handbook-build-text:
Place the stand and finish it with right clicks while holding the part, in this order:
1. 2 iron plates
2. 2 mill rolls
3. A screwdown
4. An iron rod (the crank)
Mill rolls are forged on an anvil from a steel ingot, the screwdown from tin bronze.
rollingmill-handbook-use-text:
Right click the mill to open its window. Pick "Sheet" or "Rods", put in an ingot, look at the crank and hold right click.
Instead of the crank you can bring a mechanical power axle to the crank side: the crank comes off and the mill rolls on its own while the axle turns.
More: the Rolling mill guide.
